identity.title: Outflow structure and velocity field of Orion source. I. ALMA imaging of SiO isotopologue maser and thermal emission

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using Science Verification data from the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA), we have identified and imaged five rotational transitions

evidence.quote: Radio Source I in the Becklin-Neugebauer/Kleinmann-Low (BN/KL) region (d=418$\pm$6 pc; (cite: Kim08))
Radio Source I in the Becklin-Neugebauer/Kleinmann-Low (BN/KL) region (d=418$\pm$6 pc; (cite: Kim08))

question.value: What are the large-scale structure and velocity field of the Source I outflow in Orion BN/KL as traced by SiO isotopologues, and is the J=5-4 v=1 emission maser?

evidence.quote: Our main goal was to study in detail the large-scale structure and velocity field of the Source I outflow.
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.99001.CSV
covered the frequency range 214-246 GHz which corresponds to the lower 2/3 of the total frequency range in ALMA Band 6

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 20 spectral windows of 1.875 GHz, 3840 channels of 488.281 kHz, ~0.7 km/s Hanning-smoothed

evidence.quote: Each spectral window consists of 3840 channels that are 488.281 kHz wide.
16 antennas (each 12 meters in diameter) were included in the compact Early Science (ES) Cycle 0 configuration.
This provided a synthesized beam of $\sim$1$\ensuremath{''}$7 $\times$ 1$\ensuremath{''}$2 at a P.A. of $\sim$1$^{\rm o}$.
was conducted on 2012 January 20

what.value: CARMA SiO v=0 J=2-1 total intensity contours

evidence.quote: overlaid with the contours of the total intensity of the $^{28}$SiO v=0 J=2-1 emission as observed by (cite: Plambeck09) using CARMA

what.value: Ammonia column density map of the hot core

evidence.quote: overlaid with contours of the ammonia column density map (cite: Goddi11b) tracing dense gas in the hot core region

archive_products_used_as_is.value: SV data calibrated prior to public release

evidence.quote: The ALMA SV data were calibrated prior to public release.

flux_calibrator.value: Callisto absolute flux; J0607-085 (1.4 Jy) bandpass and phase

evidence.quote: Callisto served as the absolute flux calibrator and the quasar J0607-085, with a flux of 1.4 Jy, was used as both bandpass and phase calibrator.

self_calibration.value: single step phase-only on strongest emission feature in each cube; more steps did not help

evidence.quote: In each data cube, we used the strongest emission feature to perform a single step, phase-only self-calibration.
used the *uvcontsub* task which fits a model to the continuum and subtracts it afterwards
a Briggs weighting with a robustness parameter of 1
we used a pixel size of 0$\ensuremath{''}$3
an imagesize of 30$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 30$\ensuremath{''}$

line_free_channels.value: identified per spectral window but ranges not given

evidence.quote: We identified all channels with no line emission in each spectral window containing an SiO line

final_rms.value: ~0.01 Jy/beam line-free; up to 0.3 Jy/beam in strongest channels

evidence.quote: The rms noise in the line-free channels was about 0.01 Jy beam$^{-1}$ while it was up to 0.3 Jy beam$^{-1}$ in the channels with the strongest emission.

analysis_steps.goal: Continuum subtraction and cleaning of SiO cubes

method.value: uvcontsub on line-free channels, clean with Briggs weighting, one phase-only self-cal

evidence.quote: The first step of the SiO line imaging process was the continuum subtraction.
a pixel size of 0$\ensuremath{''}$3, an imagesize of 30$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 30$\ensuremath{''}$ and a Briggs weighting with a robustness parameter of 1

validation.value: further self-cal steps tested, no significant improvement

evidence.quote: Tests with further steps of self-calibration did not improve the image quality significantly.

analysis_steps.goal: Gaussian fits to v=1 emission per channel

method.value: 2-D elliptical Gaussian fit in each channel above 4 sigma in at least six connected pixels; errors 0.5*beam/SNR

evidence.quote: Relative positional errors are given by $\delta \theta=0.5\theta_B/SNR$, where $\theta_B$ is the FWHM of the synthesized beam.
we fitted a two-dimensional elliptical Gaussian model to the unresolved emission, in every velocity channel

validation.value: compared with J=1-0 maser structure of Matthews10

evidence.quote: The velocity structure obtained from our Gaussian fits is consistent with the one found for the masing $^{28}$SiO v=1 and v=2 J=1-0 transitions by (cite: Matthews10)

method.value: moment 0 over -20 to 40 km/s; moment 1 with 4 sigma threshold

evidence.quote: The moment 0 map is obtained integrating the emission at each pixel in the velocity range from -20 to 40 km s$^{-1}$

validation.value: compared with CARMA J=2-1 and J=8-7 SiO features to exclude contaminants

evidence.quote: we exclude contamination from other molecular species, i.e. they must be associated with SiO emission.

method.value: Tb=(S lambda^2)/(2 k_B dOmega); lower limit for unresolved v=1, integrated over source size for v=0

evidence.quote: $T_b=(S\lambda^2)/(2k_Bd\Omega)$, where $S$ is the flux, $\lambda$ the wavelength and $d\Omega$ the solid angle of the source.
For imaging we used the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA).
we derive a brightness temperature $T_b\sim$580 K
We obtained brightness temperatures of $\sim$50 K and $\sim$100 K for the $^{28}$SiO and the $^{29}$SiO isotopologue, respectively.
Errors range from 10 mas for the brightest channels to 50 mas in the channels with weakest emission.

findings_qualitative.value: Ground-state SiO traces a bipolar NE-SW outflow with complex large-scale velocity structure (blue arc, red arm, high-velocity wing) likely due to environment interaction

evidence.quote: the large scales (500-5000 AU) probed by thermal SiO with ALMA reveal a complex structure and velocity field

claims.hypothesis: Does the large-scale outflow show rotation?
claims.experiment: Moment maps of 28SiO and 29SiO J=5-4 compared with IR sources and ammonia
claims.result: Blue-red asymmetry attributable to environment and contaminants
claims.finding: No evidence for rotation on thousands-of-AU scales

evidence.quote: we exclude the presence of a velocity gradient perpendicular to the outflow axis as well as evidence of outflow rotation on scales of thousands of AU from Source I.

claims.experiment: Line widths and per-channel Gaussian positions
claims.result: Narrow peaks (~3.5 km/s), distribution like J=1-0 maser, Tb>=580 K
claims.finding: First evidence of >200 GHz SiO maser at Source I

evidence.quote: These elements provide first evidence that the v=1 J=5-4 $^{28}$SiO transition is a maser.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Two bipolar outflows, rotation, and precession rejected to explain velocity structure

evidence.quote: but it is inconsistent with the strong evidence that Source I is a hard binary

limitations_admitted.value: Vibrationally excited emission unresolved at ~1.7"x1.2"; maser nature needs confirmation

evidence.quote: If confirmed, this would be the first detection of high-frequency SiO maser emission

referee_caveats_inferred: Brightness temperatures depend on unspecified source sizes
Maser claim rests on indirect arguments

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA Science Verification data, publicly released

evidence.quote: The ALMA SV data were calibrated prior to public release.

reproducibility.score_reason: Public SV data, partial imaging recipe, qualitative main results.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results largely qualitative and several imaging parameters unstated.
